items.title: Houston Person Part 1 interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Majesty of the Seas, May 29, 1995…
items.q: They took me under their wings and helped me a lot.

ctx.x: Was I correct in reading that during the military service you got to play with quite a few people that later on became good jazz musicians also?
Oh, yeah, well they were great jazz musicians when I met them — Eddie Harris, Cedar Walton, Leo Wright, Don Menza.

items.title: Houston Person Part 2 interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 2, 1998 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: Houston grew up in South Carolina and was fortunate to play with future jazz greats Eddie Harris and Cedar Walton while in the military.

ctx.x: Houston Person is a tenor saxophonist who is equally comfortable in a jazz quartet or with an organ based trio that leans towards R&B. Born in 1934, Houston grew up in South Carolina and was fortunate to play with future jazz greats Eddie Harris and Cedar Walton while in the military. He later attended the Hartt School of Music and toured with a number of organ trios. Houston has recorded numerous albums as a leader and enjoys a longtime collaboration with singer Etta Jones.
